text.p: These are the leading stories in the Ugandan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The government of the Buganda monarchy gives a Korean developing a fish tinning factory in Munyonyo, a traditional Buganda site, 14 days to quit.
- People linked to the Allied Democratic Front rebels threaten to attack Kabale.
- A minister of state for regional cooperation says she is sceptical about Sudan honouring resolutions made at the Inter-Governmental Authority on Development meeting in Nairobi.
- President Yoweri Museveni says he is considering charging former dictator Idi Amin Dada with crimes against humanity.
- A former arch-rival of the chairman of the Democratic Party says he is ready to take over party leadership.
- Vice-President Specioza Kazibwe blames advancing desert for poverty in the country.
- All night meetings are banned in Mbarara district in western Uganda following threats of a rebel attack on the area.
- At least 100 people are arrested in the northern district of Gulu. ($1=1075 Ugandan Shillings)
